newsitem.title: UK: Funds heavily overweight sterling - Merrill survey.
newsitem.headline: Funds heavily overweight sterling - Merrill survey.

text.p: Fund managers reporting overweight currency exposure in sterling rose sharply to record levels in November and could signal a near-term top for the pound against the dollar in particular, according to Merrill Lynch's quarterly global investor survey.

The survey, which polled 104 large international investors round the world, showed that sterling's overweight reading rose from 52 in August to 64 in November - sterling's highest reading since the survey began in 1989.
A reading at 50 would indicate a net neutral positioning.

"Heavily overweight sterling readings from our Global Investor Survey and extreme bullishness on market sentiment indicators show sterling/dollar may be close to an interim top," said Joe Prendergast, foreign exchange strategist at Merrill Lynch in London.
Sterling rose up to 10 percent against the dollar between August and November, peaking at $1.6901 last week.
Elsewhere, the Merrill survey showed overall dollar exposure fell further to 58 in November from 60 in August. It is now down nine points from 67 in May.

Overall German mark exposure fell eight points to 47 from 55 over the three months, reflecting the recent rise in demand for convergence trades in higher-yielding European currencies, Merrill said. These higher-yielding units as a bloc, including the Italian lira and Spanish peseta, rose to 48 in November from 42 in August.
Canadian dollar exposure surged to 60 from 49. Japanese yen exposure fell for the first time in three quarters.
